subject: Post-call recap: dedicated inference reservation & isolation runway
messages:
From: Priyom Das <pri@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nebulatech.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nebulatech.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: dedicated inference reservation & isolation runway

Hi Alex / Sanjay — thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the handful of things we aligned on, plus next steps. I wanted to capture the details we discussed so we have a single source of truth for procurement and ops.

Key pain points you shared
- Latency variance at peak (p95 spikes from 150ms to 700ms under nightly jobs) that drives customer churn.
- Cost unpredictability when on preemptible cloud capacity; engineering time spent tuning batching.
- Regulatory need to isolate PHI-containing workloads in a tenant-bounded environment for upcoming pilots.
- Predictable burst capacity for scheduled fine-tuning and nightly scoring jobs (multiple-hour windows).

Goals we agreed on
- Proof-of-concept: Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) to validate p95 < 200ms for inference at production mix.
- Isolation: Dedicated tenant slice with encrypted KV caches and customer-managed keys for PHI pipelines.
- Scaling plan: baseline reserved pool to cover steady-state + burst pool that can scale to 2.5x for nightly jobs.
- SLOs: target 99.9% availability, p95 latency guardrails, and token-cost guidance for 6 months.

Technical constraints you flagged
- Primary region: us-west-2; secondary failover in us-east-1.
- Models: mix of 13B and 70B quantized variants; KV-cache warmup is important for short-turn queries.
- Data residency: logs/audit and KV caches must remain in your VPC until sanitized.

Preliminary capacity sketch (attachment: 2025-09-14_Nebula_capacity_calc.xlsx)
- Baseline: 8x A100 (reserved) sized to sustain 250 concurrent small-chat sessions with 2K seqs.
- Burst lane: autoscale permits additional 12x GPUs for scheduled windows (pay-for-burst model).

Next steps (action owners and timeline)
- Priyom: Share SOW draft and capacity calc (attached) by EOD 9/15.
- Alex: Confirm procurement timeline and necessary PO/contact by 9/19.
- Evelyn (ops): Follow up with a brief ops runbook and isolation checklist by 9/17.
- Technical deep-dive: schedule 60-min session with Nebula infra + our runtime team week of 9/22.

If any item above is off, please flag. Otherwise I’ll take the SOW -> pricing draft to your legal/procurement thread and loop in our security SME for the isolation checklist.

Thanks,
Priyom

Priyom — thanks for the clean writeup. Confirming a few clarifications so our procurement path matches the technical ask: 

1) Baseline sizing: the 8x A100 you sketched assumes average request sizes we shared in the doc (median 300 tokens). Can you call out expected p95 token-latency for the 13B quantized path specifically? We want a hard number for our SLA table.
2) Burst billing: can we get an option that caps daily burst spend for the pilot? Our finance team needs a guardrail before we sign anything.
3) Isolation: we will want the option to bring the pool on-prem for the long-term roadmap, but pilot should be VPC-connected hosted.

Procurement cadence: we expect to open a PO the week of 9/29 if the SOW and pricing land this week and security checks are green. I’ve added Sanjay here — he’ll coordinate PO and procurement questions.

Quick ask: Please send the SOW draft and a single-paragraph security summary we can share with our compliance team.

— Alex

Alex — glad to meet you. Short ops notes and answers to your asks so the procurement and compliance threads are served: 

- p95 token-latency (13B quantized): expected 140–220ms for the request profile you shared with a warmed KV cache. We will include bench runs in the technical deep-dive to show variance under the production mix.
- Burst cap: we can propose a soft cap billing fence that alerts and requires explicit approval once the burst run rate crosses a pre-agreed monthly threshold. That’s an acceptable commercial construct for pilots; we’ll capture it in SOW language.
- Isolation: pilot model — hosted in your VPC (private deployment) with customer-managed KMS for encryption of KV caches and audit logs. On-prem migration is supported via our Private package; we’ll list migration milestones and data transfer controls in the SOW.

Operational checklist I’ll produce for 9/17 (will include runbook items: KV-cache priming, prefix-caching rules, model variant fallback, and how to failover to the burst lane with minimal latency impact).

Vivek — I’ve included you for pricing/commits guidance; will hand off SOW questions to finance.

— Evelyn
